Summary:
- Large media archive (news footage + transcripts + metadata) aiming to modernize search for editorial and compliance teams. Primary goal: high-recall retrieval + precise reranking for user-facing search UI.
- Corpus: ~1.2B tokens raw; ingest plan yields ~14M chunks (avg 700 tokens after scene-aware chunking).
- Current infra: on-prem object store + PostgreSQL metadata; exploring Redwood Dedicated in VPC for inference close to storage.

Technical requirements / priorities:
- Embedding index scale: expect 10-20M vectors to start, grow to 50M in 12 months. Need cost estimate per qps and storage.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms for query path (embedding lookup + reranker top-30 cross-encode) — editorial UX sensitive.
- Cost target: <$0.02 per query (analytics-backed target) including embedding retrieval + reranker compute.
- Reranker: team prefers a two-stage ranker: fast sparse/hybrid retriever -> bi-encoder vector shortlist -> cross-encoder rerank (fine-tune on editor relevance labels). Want Redwood suggestions for quantized cross-encoder and CPU fallback.
- Chunking strategy: experimenting with scene/paragraph boundary-aware chunking rather than fixed 512 tokens; target overlap 80-150 tokens. Concern: recall drop if chunk granularity too coarse (missed anchor spans).
- QA/labels: have ~5k human relevance labels from editors, willing to run small active learning loop for reranker fine-tune.
- Ingest pipeline must preserve timestamps, program_ids, transcript speaker segments to support contextual filters.
